raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Split from #41994 as requested in review: the batch < 64 part. The other parts are #42280 (`MinFreeSlotsDelayer`) and #42281 (DSpark verify width).

## Motivation

With overlap scheduling and speculative decoding on HIP, `FutureMap.resolve_seq_lens_cpu` and `resolve_mixed_spec_tails` block the host on the previous forward's publish event (`publish_ready.synchronize()`, #26672), so the GPU idles between the DSpark verify and the next draft. Event-timed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (on the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD development branch), that idle was 0.65 ms of an 8.9 ms batch-1 cycle.

The host sync exists because `Event.wait()` on the separate schedule stream is slower still: a device wait pending in another HIP queue while a graph runs slows every dispatch of that graph (on MI355X a 512-kernel graph takes 1541 us instead of 853 us with such a wait pending). In the same timing, replacing the sync with that wait alone removed 0.50 ms of the idle but made the verify graph 1.21 ms slower.

`needs_cpu_seq_lens` does not reach this sync. The DeepSeek-V4.1 HIP backend already sets it to False on main (#41308 derives it from `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS`, off by default). On the Low-Latency DSpark cell on main `dcf4e18283`, a print-only probe shows `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` for both the target and the draft `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend`, and `resolve_seq_lens_cpu` taking the host `synchronize()` with no seq_lens D2H: on HIP the sync runs before the flag is checked. The probed files are unchanged on current main.

## Modifications

On HIP with overlap scheduling, speculative decoding and no pipeline parallelism, the scheduler runs on the forward stream (`Scheduler.schedule_on_forward_stream`, decided once in `init_overlap`), and `FutureMap(same_queue_publish=True)` waits on the publish event in-queue with `Event.wait()` instead of blocking the host. Stream order carries the forward-to-schedule dependencies. Without speculation there is no publish wait, so the separate schedule stream stays. CUDA is unchanged; on HIP this applies to every speculative algorithm.

## Accuracy Tests

- Batch 1, 64 fixed GSM8K questions and 8 retrieval probes per server: every server scored 62/64 and 8/8 in both arms on main `dcf4e18283` (61-63/64 and 8/8 in an earlier session on main `a702970ecb`). Every Low-Latency server scored 63/64.
- Because this covers every speculative algorithm on HIP, the speculative AMD CI tests ran locally on MI355X with `scripts/ci/amd` and the `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x-20260930` image, on #41994's tree: `test_basic_sanity_eagle3`, `test_dflash`, `test_eagle_dp_attention` (4 GPUs), `test_frozen_kv_mtp`, `test_spec_standalone_extra`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath`, `test_build_eagle_tree` and `test_resolve_swa_kv_pool` pass. `test_adaptive_speculative` is flaky on main as well: it passed 11 of 12 runs there and 10 of 11 on main, and both failures were the same `Never downshifted` check. `mock_model/test_e2e_spec_eagle` hits a memory fault in `ck_tile::FmhaBatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel` at the same prefill on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x MI355X (gfx950), TP4/EP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `dba1be0a`, the MI350X cookbook Low-Latency cell (DSpark block 5, decode graphs up to 128) with `docker/rocm.Dockerfile`'s runtime environment and AITER as that main's Dockerfile pins it. A fresh server per arm in ABBA order, real acceptance, radix cache flushed before every measured request, no profiler during timing. Measured in #41994, whose other two changes (#42280, #42281) do not act here: the verify width is off by default, and the min-free-slots delay only acts with fewer than 4 of the 256 request slots free.

| Workload | Metric | main | This change | Change (95% CI) | Earlier session |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Batch 1, 4 real-text 4K prompts x 24 per server, 1024 tokens | decode tok/s | 363.5 | 380.0 | +4.55% [+3.56, +5.54] | +6.11% [+4.70, +7.38] |
| | wall per verify | 8.96 ms | 8.55 ms | | 9.18 ms / 8.60 ms |
| Batch 8, distinct real-text 4K prompts, 1024 tokens | verify cycles/s | 68.15 | 69.61 | +2.15% [+1.36, +2.63] | +4.32% [+3.58, +4.83] |
| Batch 32 | verify cycles/s | 43.67 | 44.58 | +2.10% [+1.65, +2.55] | +3.07% [+2.59, +3.51] |
| Batch 64 | verify cycles/s | 31.84 | 32.25 | +1.26% [+1.13, +1.40] | +1.83% [+1.44, +2.38] |

The main columns are main `dcf4e18283` with AITER `e7d2453f`; the earlier session is main `a702970ecb` with AITER `acf8fdf9`, where main's own batch-1 verify was slower (9.18 ms) while this change stayed at about 8.6 ms. Batched rows compare verify cycles per second (decode tok/s / (batch x accept length), inside the window where every request is decoding) because batched outputs, and with them acceptance, vary between runs in both arms.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

         req_to_token_pool: ReqToTokenPool,
         needs_cpu_seq_lens: bool = True,

+        same_queue_publish: bool = False,
     ):
         # Bufs indexed by req_pool_idx; slot 0 mirrors KV padding row so
         # CUDA-graph padded batches (req_pool_idx == 0) are harmless.
@@ -266,6 +267,9 @@ def __init__(
         # full decision (per-backend flag + TBO / piecewise CG overrides).
         self.needs_cpu_seq_lens = needs_cpu_seq_lens
         self.needs_confidence_relay = needs_confidence_relay
+        # True when the scheduler runs on the publishing (forward) stream, so a
+        # publish wait never crosses HW queues.
+        self.same_queue_publish = same_queue_publish
         self.req_pool_size = req_to_token_pool.req_to_token.shape[0]
         # Kept for the mixed-tail late binding (reserved-slot gather).
         self.req_to_token = req_to_token_pool.req_to_token
@@ -475,7 +479,7 @@ def resolve_mixed_spec_tails(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> None:
         if n == 0:
             return
         if self.publish_ready is not None:
-            if _is_hip:
+            if _is_hip and not self.same_queue_publish:
                 self.publish_ready.synchronize()
             else:
                 self.publish_ready.wait()
@@ -527,7 +531,7 @@ def resolve_seq_lens_cpu(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> None:
                 # forward publish; a stale consume means a publish went missing.
                 assert self._publish_fresh, "resolve without a fresh forward publish"
                 self._publish_fresh = False
-            if _is_hip:
+            if _is_hip and not self.same_queue_publish:
                 # Temporary workaround: Event.wait() regresses TPOT on AMD MI355.
                 self.publish_ready.synchronize()
             else:

@@ -1630,11 +1630,22 @@ def init_overlap(self):
             attn_backends = (self.tp_worker.model_runner.attn_backend,)
         needs_cpu_seq_lens = decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens(attn_backends)
         needs_confidence_relay = decide_needs_confidence_relay()
+        # A device wait pending in another HIP queue slows every dispatch of the
+        # forward graph running meanwhile, so speculative overlap schedules on the
+        # forward stream; without speculation there is no publish wait, and the
+        # separate schedule stream keeps overlapping the next batch's preparation.
+        self.schedule_on_forward_stream = (
+            _is_hip
+            and self.enable_overlap
+            and self.spec_algorithm.is_some()
+            and get_parallel().pp_size == 1
+        )
         self.future_map = self.spec_algorithm.create_future_map(
             self.device,
             self.req_to_token_pool,
             needs_cpu_seq_lens=needs_cpu_seq_lens,
             needs_confidence_relay=needs_confidence_relay,
+            same_queue_publish=self.schedule_on_forward_stream,
         )

                 )
+        if self.schedule_on_forward_stream:
+            self.schedule_stream = self.forward_stream
         # The global WAR barrier fences the scheduler's next shared-buffer write

         self._war_barrier_enabled = is_cuda() or envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER.get()
